title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: This entry describes ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17). I do not reliably remember the causal gene, the inheritance pattern or the reports behind this entry.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations is abbreviated ECTD17.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Only the abstract was supplied. It covers LEF1 regulation of Dll1 in mouse somitogenesis and never mentions ectodermal dysplasia-17 or the abbreviation ECTD17.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a form of ectodermal dysplasia. Ectodermal dysplasias affect structures that develop from the ectoderm, such as hair, teeth, nails and sweat glands. As the name of this entry indicates, some patients also have limb malformations. I do not remember the specific features, the causal gene or the original reports well enough to describe them.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a form of ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a syndrome that includes ectodermal dysplasia, but it does not name it ECTD17.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasias affect structures that develop from the ectoderm, such as hair, teeth, nails and sweat glands.
checks.evidence_quote: Both pathways are involved in signal transduction from ectoderm to mesenchyme during the development of ectoderm-derived structures.
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to ectoderm-derived structures and describes effects on teeth (oligodontia), hair (hypotrichosis) and sweating (hypohidrosis). Nails are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Some patients with ectodermal dysplasia-17 (ECTD17) have limb malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotypic spectrum includes various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly or split hand/foot, and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists limb malformations as part of the phenotypic spectrum. It does not say explicitly that only some patients have them, and it does not use the name ECTD17.
